items.prose: Capacity 3, each value equal to its key. Operations: put 2, put 4, put 6, get 2, put 8. Then get 4, get 6, put 10, get 2, get 8.
items.question: What is the sum of the get results? A miss returns -1.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write the order after every call.

byKey.zero: You counted each miss as 0. A miss returns -1.
byKey.never: You never evicted. Capacity 3 forces out the least recently used on puts 8 and 10.

explain.text: After put 8 the order is 8, 2, 6, so key 4 is gone. After put 10 it is 10, 6, 8, so key 2 is gone. The gets are 2, -1, 6, -1, 8, which sum to 14.

items.question: Capacity 3. Put 12, 15 and 11, then get 12, then put 14. Which key was evicted?

options.why: You evicted the oldest put. The get of 12 made it recent.
You evicted the newest put. LRU drops the oldest use.
Key 14 is the new key. It goes in, not out.

feedback.correct: The order was 11, 15, 12, then 12, 11, 15: key 15 was last.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write the order after each call.

byKey.b: The get refreshed key 12, so it is the most recent.
byKey.c: Key 11 is the second most recent after the get.
byKey.d: The put adds key 14. Something else leaves.

explain.text: After the puts the order is 11, 15, 12. The get of 12 makes it 12, 11, 15. The put of 14 drops the last, key 15.

items.prose: A TTL cache with capacity 2 and `ttl` 3. Key 1 is put at time 0. Then it is read at times 2, 5, 6 and 9.
items.question: How many of the gets return -1?

feedback.correct: The get at 2 hits and refreshes. The gets at 5, 6 and 9 miss.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find each entry's age at each get.

byKey.one: You counted only the miss at 5. The entry stays gone, so the gets at 6 and 9 miss too.
byKey.none: You never expired anything. The entry is gone once its age reaches the `ttl`.

explain.text: The get at 2 has age 2, so it hits and refreshes the entry to time 2. At 5 the age is 3, which equals the `ttl`, so the entry is gone. The gets at 6 and 9 find nothing.

items.prose: A desk buys 200 shares at £20, buys 100 at £23, then sells 250 at £25.
items.question: Under FIFO, what does the sale realise, in £?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Sell the oldest lot first.

byKey.average: You used the average cost of £21. FIFO uses each lot's own price.
byKey.newest: You sold from the £23 lot first. FIFO starts with the oldest shares.

explain.text: The sale of 250 takes all 200 shares at £20, then 50 at £23. That realises $200 \times (25 - 20) + 50 \times (25 - 23) = 1{,}100$. The average cost of £21 would give 1,000.

items.question: Why does `trade(symbol, qty, price=0)` keep the stage 1 tests passing?

options.text: Old calls pass two arguments; the default fills the third.
Python quietly ignores any extra arguments in a call.
options.why: You mixed up extra and missing. Python raises an error for extra arguments.

options.text: The old tests are skipped once the signature changes.
options.why: They are run again. That is how a break would show.

options.text: A `price` argument is optional in every language.
options.why: An argument is optional only when the signature gives it a default.

feedback.correct: The default makes the new argument optional.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the arguments in the old call.

byKey.b: The old call has too few arguments, not too many.
byKey.c: Running the old tests is the check.
byKey.d: Optional arguments exist only with a default value.

explain.text: The old call passes two arguments. With `price=0` the third is optional, so Python fills it in. Without the default the call raises `TypeError`.

items.prose: One user, limit 3, window 7. Requests arrive at times 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 and 8. A refused request is not recorded.
items.question: How many requests are accepted?

feedback.correct: T, T, T, F, F, T, T: five accepted.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Drop old times before each decision.

byKey.edge: You kept the time 0 alive at 7. The cut-off is 0, and 0 is not above 0.
byKey.recorded: You recorded the refused requests at 3 and 4, so the log stayed full.

explain.text: The times 0, 1 and 2 are accepted, and 3 and 4 are refused. At 7 the time 0 has left, so 7 is accepted. At 8 the time 1 has left, so 8 is accepted.

items.prose: A token bucket has capacity 4 and rate 2. Requests arrive at times 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2 and 9.
items.question: How many requests are accepted?

widget.label: Accepted
widget.accept: 8: four at time 0, two at 1, one at 2 and one at 9

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the refill before each time's requests.

byKey.noRefill: You gave the bucket no refill. It adds 2 tokens a second.
byKey.all: You accepted every request. The fifth at time 0 and the third at time 1 meet an empty bucket.

explain.text: Time 0 spends all 4 tokens and refuses the fifth request. Time 1 adds 2 tokens, so 2 pass and the third is refused. Time 2 adds 2 and one passes, and by time 9 the bucket is full again.

items.prose: A hit counter only needs the last 300 seconds. It keeps a ring of 300 buckets, one per second.
items.question: What does the ring cost as traffic grows?

options.text: A constant 300 slots, however many hits arrive
Memory that grows with the number of hits
options.why: You stored every hit. The ring stores one count per second slot.

options.text: Memory that grows with the seconds since the start
options.why: Slots are reused as time wraps round, so old seconds are overwritten.

options.text: Memory that grows with the busiest second
options.why: A slot holds one number, whether it counts 1 hit or 1,000.

feedback.correct: The ring never grows: 300 slots of two numbers.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the slots, not the hits.

byKey.b: A busy second adds to one counter. It adds no slot.
byKey.d: A counter stores one number whatever its size.

explain.text: A ring of 300 slots keeps one count per second of the last 300 seconds. A new second overwrites the slot of the second 300 earlier. So memory is fixed.
